articleTitle: Teamwork Skills Development in the Chem-E-Car Competition(R) at the Universidad Nacional de San Antonio Abad Del Cusco as Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Teamwork is one of the main skills that an engineer has to manage in a work place in order to achieve professional targets. For that reason, engineering students need to cultivate and develop this ability throughout projects and competitions during their academic training. For example, in the field of chemical engineering there is a competition called Chem-E-Car competition<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(R)</sup> that is a competition of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE). Where students engage in designing and building a car powered by a chemical energy source that will safely run a specific distance and stop. The students from the Universidad Nacional de San Antonio Abad del Cusco (UNSAAC), specifically from AIChE-UNSAAC student chapter decided to participate in the Chem-E-Car competition<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(R)</sup> and assume roles for the design and construction of a Zn-air battery as a propulsion reaction and an iodine-vitamin C reaction as a stop reaction. Integrating all the reactions in a motor using electrical connections, Arduino UNO, and accessories built by 3D printing. At all stages of the competition, students developed their teamwork skills such as showing respect for other team members, demonstrating commitment to team success, and resolving differences to benefit entire team. It was reflected through observation, a checklist of deliverables, and a teamwork survey. At the end, students from the AIChE-UNSAAC student chapter participated in the 4th AIChE Latin America Student Regional Conference (PROCESA) with its prototype car, receiving the 3rd place.

articleTitle: The Impact of Faculty Competencies on Engineering Education: Strategies for Continuous Improvement and Quality Assurance Within the Accreditation Process
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This research examines the alignment level of the skills and abilities of 23 professors from the Electronic Engi-neering academic program at the Faculty of Sciences and Engi-neering of the University of Sciences and Humanities. For this purpose, a list of courses from the academic program taught in the last three semesters (2022–1, 2022–2, and 2023–1) was compiled and categorized according to thematic areas related to the academic program. Subsequently, a scale from 1 to 5 was designed, and based on the analysis of the curricula vitae and re-sumes of each professor, the professional alignment level with the thematic area each professor is responsible for was established. This analysis allowed the development of improvement plans to meet the skills and competencies related to each category and subject. Finally, this information is of particular importance within the framework of the accreditation process in which the program is currently undergoing.

articleTitle: Management of Accredited Academic Programs through the Application of Data Envelope Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The overall objective was to apply data envelope analysis (hereinafter DEA) to improve the management of accredited academic programs. The research approach was quantitative with the inductive-deductive method, explanatory level, and quasi-experimental design. The population and sample were the seven accredited academic programs of the Faculty of Engineering of Continental University. The technique for data collection were surveys and the review of information, the instrument was the questionnaire and observation sheets. It was concluded that the management of accredited academic programs of the Continental University presents differences before and after applying for DEA, which can be interpreted as significantly improving the management of accredited academic programs of the Continental University.

articleTitle: A Framework for an Automated Assessment System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The motivation for yearly assessment of student outcomes, as part of the continuous improvement process, to facilitate informed decisions for enhancing student success. A significant component of ABET accreditation is implementing this assessment, but it remains problematic due to faculty perceptions of externally-defined rules that require significant additional work, as well as the notion that it is not part of the faculty member's core activities. To address this, we worked to create a primarily automated system that minimizes additional workload for the faculty. Coupled with ongoing discussion emphasizing the importance of assessment of student outcomes, we arrived at MSA<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the Michigan System for Automated Accreditation Assessment. Using commonly available technologies, our system improves upon prior work by increasing the level of automation and functionality while reducing faculty workload and preserving security of student information.

articleTitle: Coping Styles in Electronic Engineering Students Who Present Academic Stress in the Subject Scientific Research Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This research has made it possible to establish the way students of the Scientific Research Methodology career of the Electronic Engineering academic program of the Universidad de Ciencias y Humanidades have been coping with the academic stress caused by the characteristics of the post-pandemic context, the academic rigor of the courses in the final part of the program and the characteristics that the courses on research topics represent for the undergraduate student; to make feedback at the level of the direction of the academic program and to be able to promote a set of strategies to improve the control at an emotional level in the students to assure the quality of the program with a view to accreditation processes. A sample size made up of a total of thirty university students, between 17 and 27 years of age, enrolled in the course, which belongs to the seventh cycle of the academic program, was addressed.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Model for Predicting Academic Success Through Multi-Criteria Admissions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Academic success has been under study for several years. University students are vulnerable to problems affecting their academic background, in some cases even dropping out. The present research analyzed the academic success of those entering the UNCP taking aspects of the school trajectory, sociodemographic level, academic competencies, and extracurricular achievements. The methodology selected was the deductive-inductive method, applied type, explanatory-predictive level, nonexperimental longitudinal cohort study design; the population chosen was 11466 admissions in the academic periods 2020-I, 2020-II, 2021-I, and 2021-II. The prediction was made using three machine learning algorithms: linear regression, decision tree, and classification; where the result was 95.44% prediction with the classification model. The indicators taken into account for the model included school trajectory (entrance grade, modalities of admission, and academic preparation), socio-demographic level (age of the entrant), academic competencies and extracurricular achievements (sports and artistic participation upon entering university), the approved credits and the average, which were obtained after the end of the first academic semester. It was possible to predict the academic success of UNCP students using machine learning tools, allowing them to detect students who might face problems in their university studies.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Digital Competences of University Professors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: In this research, we measured the digital competence levels of Peruvian university professors using the DigCompEdu framework. We use a self-assessment questionnaire proposed by the framework to collect the data directly. As a result, 47.06% professors are at the leadership level and 35.29% professors are at the expertise level. In addition, it is important to highlight that within the six areas in which the twenty-two competences are divided, the one that obtained the lowest results is area 04 called Assessment in which we recommended to improve their digital competences.

articleTitle: Evaluating Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility in Accreditation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The advantages of the current digital evolution foster the responsibility of having technical advancements, applications, and tools reflect the societal needs regarding diversity, equality, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) within disciplines and organizations. These four elements should become part of all accreditation criteria and processes for engineering, computing, and other related programs, where accreditation bodies, higher education institutions, and educators become ready to implement these elements in any new setting. This work continues the discussion of an earlier paper that addresses the meaning of three of these four concepts in the context of accreditation. It also emphasizes the potential benefits for technical professions, future engineers, and the ICACIT accrediting agency. Hence, it is essential not only to integrate diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility in higher education study programs and global accreditation criteria but also to seek both quantitative and qualitative methods to evaluate these DEIA elements to ensure all students receive the best possible university education.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Between a Traditional Design Curriculum and a Problem and Project- Based Learning (PBL) Aligned Curriculum Applied to Electromagnetism Under Systematic Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The new paradigms of Industry 4.0 and current global problems such as climate change, environmental degradation, economic development, among others, require the education of engineers focused on sustainability. At the educational level, curriculums based on active methodology are increasingly relevant. However, the discussion between the advantages of using a curriculum based on Problem based learning (PBL) or a traditional one continues until nowadays. It is frequently said using PBL, in the absence of traditional direct teaching, the student learns less. However, the present work demonstrated that PBL-based curriculum design did not reduce student scores when both approaches were subjected to systematic evaluation. A brief state of the art of current knowledge in Curriculum Design is presented. Then, the results of a systematic assessment test of both curricula are shown. This experiment was carried out in the Electromagnetism course at the University of Piura.

articleTitle: Human Centered Design for Virtual Reality and Design Science Research to Virtual Heritage – Palacio de Puruchuco
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Interactive technology is in constant evolution, it allows for new products, services, work models, and advances in all fields. The purpose of this study is to describe the method used for cultural heritage virtualization, a project developed in a collaborative effort between university researchers and the Arturo Jimenez Borja Site Museum in Lima, Peru. An iterative method based on Human centered design for virtual reality and the principles of Action Design Research was used. This document hopes to give students the artefacts necessary to develop virtual cultural heritage. Results show a method for capturing 3D data, method to develop software interfaces with virtual reality, and an instrument to measure the quality perception of a virtual heritage.

Author Keywords: human centered design for virtual reality

articleTitle: A Syllabus on Bio-Inspired Computing with Student Outcomes Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Bio-inspired algorithms is an important approach in computer science which are based on the principles of the biological evolution and animal or insect behavior. We have considered twelve of the most know bio-inspired algorithms for proposed a syllabus for undergraduate course in a computer science program. The main objective of this paper is to detail the student outcomes evaluation based on accreditation criteria for computer programs proposed by the Institute for Quality and Accreditation of Computer, Engineering and Technology Programs (ICACIT) in 2019. Furthermore, we shows the analysis and results of the student outcomes evaluation in a course of the Computer Science Program of the National University of San Agustin of Arequipa (UNSA) where we obtain over 80% between excellent and satisfactory from five of the eight performance indicators evaluated.

articleTitle: Environmental Awareness: A Quantitative Analysis in Engineering University Students
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The purpose of this research was to quantify the environmental awareness of engineering university students. In this sense, a quantitative investigation with descriptive scope and non-experimental type was established since only one measurement of the phenomenon studied was carried out. Likewise, a cross-sectional research design was used since the data collection was carried out at a specific time. A digital form with 14 questions and a Likert-type scale was used: very low (1), low (2), medium (3), high (4) and very high (5). In addition, the form had a range between 14 and 70 for the total score. The analysis of the results for each question made it possible to determine that the engineering students established a medium-high level for their knowledge and participation in environmental issues with a value of 3.44 ± 0.84 and 3.69 ± 0.83, respectively. Regarding the total scores of the questionnaire, the mean of the environmental awareness scores was 49.87 while the standard deviation was 6.97, which means that the answers of the students fluctuated mainly between 42.9 and 56.84; that is, at a medium level. In the inferential aspect, the statistical analysis did not determine significant differences regarding basic education, professional career, gender and semester of study. Finally, it was possible to conclude that environmental awareness in engineering students is located at a medium level. On the other hand, it was concluded that environmental awareness should be a relevant indicator to measure the effectiveness of environmental education at the university field.

articleTitle: Selection of a Suitable Curriculum to Study the Career of Electronic Engineering in Northern Lima Using AHP
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The need for professionals who are able to develop industries through technology in Northern Lima (NL) has increased the offering in electronic engineering career (EEC) in that area, but the educational quality and its results for future students are still uncertain. For this reason, this paper selects an academic curriculum (AC) of this career that is more suitable for future students of NL, and that maximizes their opportunities. As alternatives, the three available ACs to study this career at present in private universities in NL were presented. The analytical hierarchical process (AHP) method was applied for the selection, considering four criteria: employability, research, technology and infrastructure, and tuition fees, which were ordered hierarchically by a group of four experts in the pertinent fields. The result is that the most suitable AC for studying the EEC in NL is the third one, closely followed by the first one, and then, far away from the other two, the second one, with the specific details of the universities that offers them being provided in this article.

articleTitle: Gaps and Proposals for ICT use in Rural Quechua-Aymaras Higher Technological Education During COVID-19 Using Data Mining and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The Institutes of Higher Public Technological Education (IHPTE) of the rural environment in the Altiplano of the Puno region - Peru, located above 4000 meters above sea level, these students are going through the worst economic crisis due to social confinement in the context of the covid-19 pandemic, without minimum conditions to face the biosecurity measures to contain the massive contagion, submerged to educational abandonment, technological postponement and lack of basic services. The research aims to determine gaps and proposals for the appropriate use of Information Technologies (IT) in the IESTP of Nuñoa in the Quechua zone and in the IESTP of Ilave in the Aymara zone in the context of the pandemic, was designed a questionnaire which was validated with 0.637 Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin test (KMO) and significant Bartlett's test, was collected dataset of 416 students, employing Data Mining Techniques was selected the influential attributes for (Deserters), the results show that the influential attributes are: “Economic support”,”Source of infection”, “Synchronous Virtual Classroom”,”Use of virtual system”, “Cultural identity”,”Dimensional Cause”; considering the reduced dataset was submitted to the classification algorithms of the machine learning with the significant metrics: Decision tree J48 (Recall 81. 5%), Naive Bayes (Recall 84.7%), Support Vector Machines (Recall 83.7%), the interpreting the leaves of the J48 tree as decision rules, with which was proposed strategies to close the gaps in access to educational technology.
